title: Read-only and writable text
description:
Write in `solution.c`. Choose `const` for every pointer the function only reads through, as in the declarations:

```c
const char *skip_spaces(const char *s);    /* the first character that is not a space (isspace) */
void trim_end(char *s);                    /* removes spaces at the end, in place */
char *trim(char *s);                       /* trims the end in place and returns a pointer
                                              to the first non-space character */
int count_in(const char *s, const char *set);   /* how many characters of s appear in set:
                                                   count_in("hello", "lo") is 3 */
```
hints: A string literal like `"lo"` cannot be passed to a plain `char *` without a warning about const, which is a clue for which parameters need `const`. In `count_in`, `strchr(set, c)` tells you whether `c` is in `set`. Careful: `strchr` also "finds" the terminator, so stop at the end of `s` first.
